title: African Union Commission Internship Programme (2026 posting)
overview: Full-time, on-site internships of at least three months at the African Union headquarters in Addis Ababa for final-year students, postgraduate students and graduates from AU member states.
duration: At least 3 months, possibly extended by another 3 months
deadline_text: Posting runs from 16 February to 31 December 2026 (AU careers posting, read 5 October 2026). The au.int internship page itself states no deadline.
funding_details: AU: "AU does not provide any financial support or cover any costs for living expenses during the assignment for interns."
Travel, visas, accommodation, living expenses and medical insurance are the responsibility of interns or their sponsoring institutions.
age_requirement: Between 22 and 32 at the time of application
education_requirement: Full-time undergraduate student in the final year, postgraduate student, or graduate
nationality_requirements: Nationals of African Union member states
language_requirement: Fluent in one AU working language (Arabic, English, French, Portuguese or Kiswahili)
eligibility: Aged 22 to 32
Final-year undergraduate, postgraduate student or graduate
National of an AU member state
Fluent in one AU working language
documents_required: CV on the mandatory AU CV template
application_process: Apply through the AU careers portal with the AU CV template
potential_issues: Unpaid: interns pay their own travel, visa, housing and insurance in Addis Ababa
The AU CV template is mandatory
action: Apply on the AU careers portal before 31 December 2026 using the AU CV template, if you can cover your own costs in Addis Ababa.

title: UNON/OIF Fellowship Programme for Young African Interpreters (2026 cohort)
organization: United Nations Office at Nairobi (UNON) with the Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF)
overview: A six-week paid training fellowship in Nairobi for young African conference interpreters with French as their A or retour language who recently graduated from a PAMCIT member university.
deadline_text: "Applications must be received no later than 11:59 p.m. Nairobi time on 8 October 2026" (UNON call for applications, read 5 October 2026). An online assessment is tentatively planned for 10 October 2026.
funding_details: UNON call: "a monthly stipend of USD 3,000; a one-time settling-in grant of USD 1,300; return air travel ...; medical insurance coverage arrangements."
stipend: USD 3,000 a month plus a USD 1,300 settling-in grant
age_requirement: Under 35 at the time of application
education_requirement: Master's degree in conference interpreting from a PAMCIT member university (Nairobi, Buea, Ghana, Gaston Berger, Maputo Pedagogical), obtained within the last three years
nationality_requirements: Young African professionals; open only to graduates of PAMCIT member universities
language_requirement: French as A or retour language; English as B or C
eligibility: Under 35
Master's in conference interpreting from a PAMCIT member university within the last three years
French A or retour, English B or C
application_process: Send one PDF (motivation letter and CV in French, degree and transcripts, passport page) by email as described in the UNON call
potential_issues: Only for graduates of five PAMCIT universities, none of them in the DRC
action: Read the UNON call and apply by email before 23:59 Nairobi time on 8 October 2026 if you hold a PAMCIT interpreting master's.

title: D-Prize Challenge 2026/2027
overview: Grants of up to USD 20,000 for new social entrepreneurs to run a three-month pilot of a proven poverty intervention in a developing country, applied for with a two-page concept note.
deadline_text: Midnight Pacific time: early submission 25 October 2026, regular submission 15 November 2026, extension deadline 6 December 2026 (D-Prize site, read 5 October 2026).
funding_details: D-Prize: "up to $20,000 USD to support a three-month pilot" for selected winners.
experience_requirement: Open to students, recent graduates, entrepreneurs and professionals; new organisations only
nationality_requirements: Winners can be from anywhere and operate in any developing country with extreme poverty
eligibility: 18 or older
New organisations only (usually under 18 months of operation and under USD 30,000 raised)
A clear plan to live and work in the country of the pilot
Must address one of D-Prize's published challenges
application_process: Choose one of the published challenges and submit a two-page concept note and résumé(s)
potential_issues: A competitive grant, not a job
You must plan to live and work where the pilot runs
action: Read the D-Prize challenges and submit a concept note by 25 October (early) or 15 November 2026.

title: Unearthodox Exploration Co-Lab 2027: Edges of Possibility
overview: A ten-month online incubation for early-stage initiatives working on environmental and societal change, with CHF 10,000 of funding and tailored non-financial support.
deadline_text: "Nov 16, 2026, 11:59 PM GMT+1" (official application portal, read 5 October 2026).
funding_details: Unearthodox: "CHF 10,000 to help move your initiative forward" plus about "CHF 60,000 in value of non-financial, tailored support" for selected initiatives.
experience_requirement: An early-stage initiative already beyond the idea stage
eligibility: Early-stage initiative at the intersection of environmental and societal change, beyond the idea stage
All activities in English
Group calls scheduled within UTC-6 to UTC+6
action: Read the open call and apply on the linked portal before 16 November 2026.

title: The Earth Prize 2027
overview: A free environmental sustainability competition for secondary-school students worldwide, individually or in teams of up to five, with USD 10,000 for each of seven regional winners.
program_dates: Winners announced 3 to 9 May 2027; ceremony 28 May 2027
deadline_text: Registration until 10 January 2027; submissions close 31 January 2027 at 12:00 PM CET (The Earth Prize site, read 5 October 2026).
funding_details: The Earth Prize rules: "Registration for The Earth Prize is free of charge. No purchase is necessary to enter or to win."
Seven regional winners receive USD 10,000 each.
education_requirement: Currently in school, homeschool or another educational programme
eligibility: Born between 2007 and 2014
Currently a student
Individuals or teams of up to 5; a mentor is optional
potential_issues: Registration closes 10 January 2027, before the submission deadline
action: Register on theearthprize.org before 10 January 2027 and submit by 31 January 2027.

title: I AM NALA Fellowship 2027
overview: A six-month online leadership fellowship for displaced African women (refugees, internally displaced or stateless) active in politics, campaigning, peacebuilding or advocacy.
program_dates: January to July 2027 (bi-monthly online sessions, possible in-person engagements)
deadline_text: 31 October 2026, on the organiser's Google Form (read 5 October 2026); shortlisted candidates notified by 6 November 2026. The call is not listed on nalafem.org.
funding_details: No amount on the application form. Reported by secondary sources: "capacity and technical support, mentorship, solidarity, access and resourcing".
experience_requirement: Leadership in politics, campaigns, peacebuilding or advocacy
nationality_requirements: African women who are refugees, internally displaced or stateless, including in the diaspora
eligibility: Woman aged 18 to 40
Refugee, internally displaced person or stateless
African, including displaced Africans in the diaspora
Leadership in politics, campaigns, peacebuilding or advocacy

The support offered is not described on the form
